findings.text: Comparing via UnixNano() overflows int64 for times outside roughly 1678–2262. For example, the zero time.Time{} (year 1) against time.Now() gives a wrong Greater/Less result, so assert.Less(time.Time{}, now) can fail or pass incorrectly. Use Before/After/Equal, or compare seconds and then nanoseconds.

obj2 is never checked for a type compatible with time.Time. If obj1 is a time.Time and obj2 is a different struct or type, obj2Value.Convert(timeType) panics instead of reporting a type mismatch. For example, Greater(time.Now(), struct{}{}) panics.

1.reason: In testify, compareTwoValues only checks that both values have the same reflect.Kind, so any struct paired with a time.Time gets to this code; the patch checks CanConvert only on obj1 and calls obj2Value.Convert(timeType) unconditionally, which panics for a non-convertible struct like struct{}{}. This is a different defect from the UnixNano overflow. The ./context/ directory was missing, so the caller check comes from knowledge of testify, not from files read here.
